papers.title: Health on the Move: The Impact of Poverty Alleviation Relocation on Healthcare Utilization in China.
papers.abstract: Limited utilization of healthcare services remains a persistent challenge for poor populations in many countries. This study examines the impact of China's Poverty Alleviation Relocation Program (PARP) on healthcare utilization, utilizing panel data from rural households in 16 counties across eight provinces. Employing a difference-in-differences (DID) framework, we find that relocation leads to a 24.6% increase in clinic visits and a 36.9% increase in hospital visits per household, helping prevent minor illnesses from escalating. Despite higher utilization, relocation does not significantly raise total medical expenditure, out-of-pocket medical costs, or reimbursement levels, due to reduced per-visit costs. Mechanism analysis suggests that relocation improves access to healthcare facilities and boosts household income. Our findings highlight the critical role of combining housing mobility with healthcare system improvements to promote healthcare equity, offering important insights for the design of poverty alleviation strategies in other developing country contexts where access to healthcare remains a critical constraint.
papers.summary: 本研究探討中國易地扶貧搬遷項目（PARP）對醫療服務利用的影響。基於8省16縣的農村家庭面板數據與雙重差分法（DID）分析，發現搬遷顯著提升家庭至診所與醫院的就診率（分別增加24.6%與36.9%），有效防止小病惡化。儘管就診頻率增加，但因單次就醫成本下降，總醫療支出、自付費用與報銷水平並未顯著增加。其背後機制在於搬遷改善了醫療設施的可及性並提升了家庭收入。
papers.significance: 此研究為發展中國家提供了關鍵的政策啟示，證明了將住房流動性（易地搬遷）與醫療體系改善相結合，能有效促進醫療公平並打破「因病致貧」的惡性循環。研究結果不僅為中國的精準扶貧政策提供了實證支持，也為其他面臨醫療資源可及性限制的開發中國家設計扶貧與公共衛生策略提供了重要參考價值。
